scope: Source lineage, prior-generation difference and recorded human studio review; hashes alone do not establish artistic independence or certify legal rights.

items.review_observations: Unequal fruit facets, short stem and leaf read across views; red peel stays distinct at native icon sizes.
Point, shaft and fletching replace the former capped stick. Supersampled native icons retain the formerly missing thin shaft.
Oval loaf and exposed cuts remain visible; underside/side are simple crust, not decorative box panels.
Real opening, rim and arched handle; side view is deliberately thin. Water-state checks are separate.
Elongated charred branch differs from lumpy coal; brighter neutral char and an exposed ash-coloured end now separate it from the dark UI background.
Unequal dark mineral lobes and angular facets read as coal; dark blue-gray is intentional, distinct from brown-gray charred wood.
Final exposed fat and localized sear bands read on top; broad organic cut differs from raw meat.
Broad bevelled cheek, socket and wooden haft; front/back distinction is intentional, no full-metal handle.
Overlapping/riveted front plates, stitched shoulder supports and side panels differ from iron ridges and gold decoration.
Hollow cuffs, layered toe plates and dark soles; copper rivets remain construction accents, not all-surface trim.
Separate crown panels and riveted brow are visible; side opening rises toward the face. Worn eye checks remain separate evidence.
Angled broad working plate with a riveted socket; recognizable hoe profile from top/side.
Bevelled billet with copper surface treatment and small stamping; shared billet archetype is intentional.
Four riveted front plates on a dark carrier, belt and buckle; the unplated rear is intentional backing.
Reinforced bridge, cast point/adze, riveted socket and wooden haft; not an iron head recolour.
Bevelled pointed blade with reinforcing socket and copper fasteners; side thickness and rear attachment read correctly.
Broad angular point, narrow dark central line and curved guard; gray view confirms a solid blade rather than a cutout.
Open polygonal coil, layered loops and loose end read in silhouette and small icons; no former plank placeholder.
Separate flint and hollow steel striker, linked at the rear; thin side view is intentional, not a missing surface.
Thin shaped cheek, decorative lozenge and collars distinguish the fragile gold tier; rear cheek is complete.
Faceted central front detail and lozenge accent with shoulder straps; plain rear panel and distinct side backing.
Front fittings, lower bands and hollow cuffs distinguish the gold construction; dark soles stay consistent.
Fine central crest and brow lozenge differ from copper paneling and iron ridge; front opening remains clear in worn tests.
Fine angled plate and narrow collars retain the hoe function without turning the haft gold.
Bevelled gold billet with restrained lozenge stamp; not an armour/utility placeholder.
Faceted plates with thin securing bands wrap front/side differently from copper rivets and iron kneecaps.
Slender asymmetrical tips, decorated spine and collars communicate a lighter construction than iron/copper.
Thin pointed blade, dark socket and fine gold framing; icon remains a shovel rather than a sword.
Bevelled point, split guard and narrow warm fuller; no former apparent hole through the blade.
Unequal gold kernels replace boxes; the grouped icon reads as grain rather than a solid ingot.
Broad forged cheek, square poll and socket over wooden handle; working bevel is visible in side/top views.
Raised front ridges, plain rear and stitched side backing form a restrained steel construction.
Steel cuffs, contrasting upper band and toe ribs are readable; openings and rear heel faces are complete.
Ridged roof, brow and cheek silhouette; eye clearance is proven separately on both worn body forms.
Forged angled working plate, wedge and socket are distinct from pickaxe and axe heads.
Bevelled steel billet with forge/stamp details; intentional shared ingot shape differs from ores.
Angled thigh and shin plates over dark backing, buckle and knee articulation; no copied copper-rivet pattern.
Asymmetric point/adze, socket pin and wood/binding remain identifiable in small icons.
Octagonal face, central boss/spine, rear handle ring and strap; actual reverse construction replaces flat trim.
Pointed steel blade and attachment socket, subtle forge marks and bindings; edge-on thinness is intentional.
Tapered solid blade, fuller line, straight guard and bound grip; geometry and steel finish are coherent.
Unequal sheet and rolled/folded edge replace a decorative rectangular material block.
Separate front/back panels, shoulder straps, seam and buckle; open sides are intentional arm/torso clearance.
Visible laces, soft leather cuffs and dark soles give a distinct nonmetal boot construction.
Open face, cheek flaps and stitched central strip read as leather headwear; deliberate gaps are not missing model parts.
Separate sewn panels, knee bands, waist stitching and buckle; seams continue across side/rear.
Tapered loose strands and central tie read as a bundle; flattened edge view is intentional.
Green mineral matrix with copper lobe and a smaller inclusion; rear matrix is plain by construction, not an untextured fallback.
Faceted pale matrix and visible gold lobe differ from iron/copper; simple rear matrix is intentional.
Rough matrix, oxide and embedded pale inclusions; no former flat rectangular applied plates.
Red irregular cut, pale fat/bone details and top marbling remain distinct from the cooked cut and bread.
Unequal brown seeds arranged as a small group, distinct from gold grain and material sheets.
Two loops, hinge and separate cutting halves; thin edge-on view is intentional, not a missing mesh.
Tapered branch with short side twig; side/top views retain a simple believable material form.
Chipped faceted cheek and lashing rather than metal socket; stone colour and grain differ from forged iron.
Knapped angled plate held by crossed binding; complete top/rear faces and wood haft.
Knapped head profile and crossing lashings distinguish it from the steel socket construction.
Stone blade with knapped inset and visible lashings; no automatic metallic handle recolour.
Faceted stone blade and wrapped lower fastening; profile and texture read as stone rather than painted steel.
Sewn flattened organic vessel, cork and neck binding; unlike bucket in every inspected view.
Laminated wooden cheek, binding and visible joinery on both faces; no steel-coloured functional parts.
Final narrow bent staves and separated string expose the gap in silhouette; full draw/contacts tested separately.
Wooden angled working member with key/bindings; top and rear construction remain readable.
Shaped laminated bridge, point/adze and spline, with wooden joinery and lashings.
Shaped plank face, painted spine, metal edge/fasteners and actual rear handle/strap; clear distinction from iron shield.
Bevelled wooden blade and binding, with grain aligned to the working member.
Separate pointed metal tip, lashing and long wooden shaft; supersampled icons retain the former missing shaft at 32 px.
Shaped wooden blade, central spline, crossguard and wrapped grip replace the plain rod.
Bound fuel head and separate faceted flame distinguish it from flint/steel; bright tip remains readable.
Unequal pale fleece lobes with a securing tie; recognisable soft bundle rather than a textured box.
